sections.what_happened: PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM: An oil tanker that had switched off its tracking systems and tried to cross a 'prohibited and dangerous area' / 'restricted and unsafe area' east of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines, was damaged and caught fire. The Iranian Navy said the Strait remains 'unsafe and closed' to vessels passing without coordination, and ships seeking safe passage must coordinate with Iran's armed forces. NO vessel identity, flag, crew number, casualty or damage detail was given in any carry.
sections.what_verified: The STATEMENT is confirmed across carries, the EVENT is not: every carry repeats the same single IRNA statement. Carrying families: IRNA (primary source), Anadolu, Al Jazeera liveblog, Gulf News liveblog, Dawn liveblog. No Reuters/AP/AFP wire confirmation, no UKMTO alert, no CENTCOM statement, no owner/insurer confirmation of a vessel, fire or mine strike was found in this window. Repetition of one statement is not independent corroboration of the event.
sections.what_disputed: No independent confirmation of any vessel, fire, mine or casualty; the statement gives no identifying detail that could be checked. Do NOT conflate with totw-20261027-1800-03 (UKMTO third-party report of a vessel on fire 63nm southeast of al-Faw, Iraq -- different location, cause unstated). No claimant number is presented as a counted number: the only counted Hormuz figure is the STALE PortWatch count below.
sections.why_matters: 'NO NAME, NO FLAG, NO CREW -- BUT A BURNING TANKER CLAIM EAST OF HORMUZ': Iran says a dark tanker hit its mines in a prohibited area. The claim, the missing ship, and the stale counted flow (4 transits on Oct 18 vs 85.5/day baseline) all on screen; nothing asserted beyond the statement.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Gulf News liveblog 17:22 ; APA 17:32 ; AJ liveblog 12:30 UTC = 16:30 ; in no prior scan as its own item) -- Iranian army/navy says oil tanker hit naval mines east of Strait of Hormuz and caught fire; no vessel, flag, crew or casualty details

totw_analysis: Our read: 'NO NAME, NO FLAG, NO CREW -- BUT A BURNING TANKER CLAIM EAST OF HORMUZ': Iran says a dark tanker hit its mines in a prohibited area. The claim, the missing ship, and the stale counted flow (4 transits on Oct 18 vs 85.5/day baseline) all on screen; nothing asserted beyond the statement. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Blockade enforcement vs freedom of navigation: is Tehran policing its own claimed waters against rule-breaking dark tankers, or mining an international strait and calling it regulation?
